column1: # The package container, as an open-source extractor reads it and as three current-generation
# Columns: struct, field, offset, size, type, value, note
# **Two different activities, and the order between them is the whole provenance argument.**
# Structure comes from source that can be named. The packages then *confirm or refute* it,
# and rows marked `measured` are ones they settled. Deriving the structure from the packages
# would be the thing principle 6 forbids; using them to check a structure taken from source
# is what `derive` already does to a finished module. (orbistoun#D181, orbistoun#D182)
# # The entry names come from LibOrbisPkg, and the derivations came first
# `LibOrbisPkg` (maxton) is an open-source PS4 packaging tool — a **writer**, which is what
# unblocked the container format too. `LibOrbisPkg/PKG/Enums.cs` names every entry id and
# `PKG/PkgBuilder.cs` says how each is produced. This repository already trusted that project
# for the fake keyset; the names below come from the same place.
# Worth recording in this order because it happened in this order: `0x1`, `0x100`, `0x80` and
# `0x1002` were derived from packages *before* the source was read, and the source then agreed
# with all four — `DIGESTS`, `METAS`, `GENERAL_DIGESTS`, `PLAYGO_CHUNK_SHA`. A derivation that
# survives meeting its source is worth more than either alone.
# # Two rows here were DERIVED rather than cited, and can be re-checked
# `entry_content` rows `0x1` and `0x100` came from no source. They were established by stating
# a hypothesis a machine can falsify and running it against every package available, which is
# the same method that settled the vendor dynamic tags (`RELA + RELASZ == HASH`) and a
# **Re-run it yourself**: `selfish derive <package> <package> ...`. It reports how many samples
# each claim survived and exits non-zero if any fails. Three packages backed both when written;
# more packages can only strengthen or kill them, and either is worth knowing.
# Both are *computable*, which is why they were worth chasing: a writer can produce them from
# data it already holds. The remaining four unknown entries are not, and are not guessed at.
# The SELF container is little-endian throughout. This one is not: magic, counts and offsets
# are all big-endian. A reader that assumes one convention across both formats gets a
# plausible-looking entry count in the tens of millions.
# # Every reference found is previous-generation, and the packages are not
# The extractor says so in its own header. That makes this table unusual for the project:
# the *structure* is previous-generation and the *confirmation* is current, so where they
# agree is evidence the format did not change, and any place they disagree is a finding
# nobody here has published. So far they agree on everything checked.
#         ->  PFS image at a fixed 0x700000, AES-XTS encrypted under ekpfs
#         ->  block 11 of that holds a PFSC (zlib-compressed) inner image
#         ->  inner PFS: the real filesystem, each executable an fSELF
# Four nested formats, not one container. Recovering `ekpfs` needs RSA-2048, SHA-256 and
# AES-CBC before any of the above can be read, and the inner filesystem needs AES-XTS and
# zlib on top. The keys are the public fake-package keyset; retail packages use a key
# nobody outside the vendor has and are out of scope in the same way retail signing is.
# # A row here that was wrong, and how
# `pfs_image_offset` was recorded as a fixed `0x700000` — taken from a previous-generation
# extractor and "confirmed" by finding high-entropy data at that offset in all three samples.
# That confirmed nothing: in an encrypted package almost every offset holds high-entropy data,
# so the check could not have come out any other way.
# The real values are `0x80000`, `0x580000` and `0x80000`, and the offset is a header field.
# The corrected rows are below. The lesson is recorded here rather than quietly fixed, because
# the failure was in the method rather than the number: the search asked whether a value that
# was already believed appeared in the header, and treated its absence as support. (D011)
# # Every container inside these packages is previous-generation
# Thirty-three of them, across all three samples, and not one carries the current generation's
# magic — including a working homebrew store for the current console. Retail material uses the
# newer format; community tooling emits the older one and the loader takes it. (D010)
# Most of the header. Only three fields are named below because only three are used by the
# reader this came from, and inventing names for the rest would be worse than leaving the
# gap visible. The body between the entry table and 0x700000 is likewise undescribed.

column1: # # The licence structure, measured from decrypted entries
# Entry 0x400 decrypts to a RIF. The offsets below are **measured** from three real licences,
# not taken from a summary: a published field list gave DiscKey at 0x1E8 and Signature at 0x2A8,
# which cannot be reconciled with the bytes and would put the signature's end 0x58 short of the
# structure. The populated region is exactly 0x260..0x400 in every sample. (D046)
# `secret_iv` is confirmed derived, not merely located: it equals the first sixteen bytes of
# sha256 of the content id padded to 48 with NULs, in every sample.
